changes_since_r45: Decision Experience Refactor: removed the R38 release-label and blanket CONFIDENCE badge from the default Supplier Request answer header; negotiation_intelligence.available is now genuinely conditional on real negotiation dimensions existing (previously hard-coded True, forcing an empty-looking negotiation card even when nothing was relevant); negotiation terminology translated to plain English (Give/Get Matrix, Dimension/Boundary/Trading Rule, Response Playbook, Escalation Triggers all renamed); removed a confirmed duplicate rendering of negotiation_dimensions; fixed a raw Python dict repr() leak in evidence_to_lead_with; renamed three internal-sounding progressive-disclosure section summaries to plain language.

Live Decision Experience Certification: audited the full Supplier Request path and found build_supplier_request_answer() (LEVERAGE, TRADE-OFF, no forced negotiation content) was fully built on the backend but never rendered on the frontend -- the same orphaned-object pattern previously found and fixed for the other three experiences. Built a six-case test matrix (A-F) and a stability test proving the deterministic composition layer behaves correctly once reached. Built tests/live_certification_harness.py -- a small, explicit, opt-in live-model certification harness (never auto-discovered by pytest, requires an explicit env-var confirmation and a real API key to run) -- but did not execute it: no live Anthropic API key exists anywhere in this environment.

Supplier Request Wiring Fix: added renderSupplierRequestAnswer(pos) to app/static/index.html and wired it into the existing render-dispatch fallback chain ahead of the generic commercial answer renderer. Supplier Request now renders its dedicated, adaptive answer object (LEVERAGE/TRADE-OFF sections that genuinely differ by case, sanitization-safe target/walk-away fields) instead of falling through to the generic template. No backend changes were required -- the backend wiring was already correct.

known_limitations: No live Anthropic API key exists anywhere in this build or the environment that produced it. Live model behavior (Parts 6-9 of the certification) remains completely unverified -- the harness to run it is included but has never been executed.

The six-case Supplier Request test matrix used mocked, prose-only evidence for its 'weak vs strong justification' distinction (Cases A/B/C/E) -- the deterministic LEVERAGE section showed identical generic facts across those cases because the kernel only reflects structured evidence, not prose. A richer test matrix with structured price-history/verification fields would better exercise this section's differentiation; not built in this pass, reported as an honest limitation rather than concealed.

Case F (routine, contract-permitted 2% adjustment) still shows a real dollar figure for the Money section -- an open, undecided design question about whether a small routine adjustment should suppress Money entirely. Not changed in this release, per explicit instruction to report it separately rather than alter behavior.

market_verification.py's and fresh_intelligence.py's shared reliance on Anthropic's server-side web_search tool remains a genuine, documented exception to full provider independence for the search mechanism itself.

The generic usefulness-scoring/composition engine remains deliberately unbuilt -- every certification finding so far has been a wiring gap or a test-data limitation, not evidence the current adaptive-composition architecture is structurally insufficient.
No live Claude/Anthropic API access exists anywhere in this build. Every test, including all HTTP-path and certification-matrix tests, is deterministic and mock-based.
